headline: Earnings jump on utility investment, lower taxes; sales flat
summary_short: Southern Company's Q2 2026 net income rose 33.4% y/y to $1,174M, and basic EPS gained 28.8% y/y to $1.03, while operating revenues were roughly flat y/y at $6,977M (+0.1%) but fell 16.9% q/q on normal winter-to-summer seasonality.
summary_long: Second-quarter revenue of $6,977M was essentially flat y/y (+0.1%) but down 16.9% q/q on normal seasonal patterns; six-month revenue was up 4.2% to $15.4B. Operating income rose 0.7% y/y to $1,776M, while net income climbed 33.4% y/y to $1,174M and basic EPS gained 28.8% to $1.03 (diluted $1.03, +30.4%). Southern attributes the earnings growth to increased investment in its state-regulated utilities, customer usage and growth, higher equity-method earnings, and lower income taxes, partially offset by higher interest expense. Non-GAAP earnings excluding items were $1.13 per share versus $0.92 a year ago. No forward guidance was issued in the release; no balance-sheet metrics were disclosed in the earnings tables.
